name: 1-Androsterone (1-Andro)

lead: 1-Androsterone (1-Andro, 1-DHEA) is an oral designer steroid sold online as a dietary supplement for muscle gain. Chemically it is an isomer of DHEA.

It is described as a prohormone converted in the body to 1-testosterone and related androgens, which act on the androgen receptor. It appears in the literature mainly through a 2011 study of a product seized by German investigators, which characterised its urinary elimination for doping control. No human trials of its effects were found.

paras: It has been sold as an oral supplement, usually in capsule products marketed to lifters. No documented routine or timeline exists.
No human safety data exist. Authorities and anti-doping bodies treat such designer androgens as pharmacologically related to anabolic steroids.

angle.text: 1-Andro is sold as a prohormone that converts to 1-testosterone and related androgens, for more muscle mass. It is known from seizure and doping-detection papers, and no human trials exist.

lead: 1-Androsterone, sold as 1-Andro or 1-DHEA, is a synthetic oral androgen that has been marketed online as a "dietary supplement" for building muscle. Chemically it is 3β-hydroxy-5α-androst-1-en-17-one, a positional isomer of the hormone DHEA [1][2]. Buyers are after the physique payoff of androgens: more lean mass, fuller shoulders and chest, and a more muscular frame.

It is described as a prohormone, meaning a compound that the body is said to convert into an active hormone, in this case 1-testosterone (dihydroboldenone) and related 1-dehydrogenated androstanes, which act on the androgen receptor [1]. A closely related product, 1-androstenediol, is also described as a prohormone of 1-testosterone that has been sold as a supplement and appears on the World Anti-Doping Agency's list of prohibited substances [3].

The compound is documented mainly in analytical chemistry. A 2011 study identified it in a product seized by German criminal investigators and characterised its urinary elimination so that anti-doping laboratories could detect it [2]. A 2019 paper described a way to measure designer steroids in supplements when reference standards are unavailable [4]. No human efficacy or safety trials were found.

paras: Wikipedia describes 1-androsterone as a prohormone that converts to 1-testosterone, 1-androstenedione and other 1-dehydrogenated androstanes, and lists it among androgen receptor agonists [1]. The published literature gives no pharmacokinetic data beyond the urinary elimination work in the 2011 identification study [2].

The authors of the 2011 identification study note that new androgen analogues never approved as drugs are marketed as supplements, mainly advertised for muscle mass, and that government authorities and WADA regard them as pharmacologically or chemically related to anabolic steroids [2]. Analytical chemists have also published methods for quantifying emerging designer steroids in supplements where reference materials are scarce [4].

In the United States, dietary supplements are sold under the 1994 Dietary Supplement Health and Education Act, which does not require government approval before sale. A 2007 to 2016 analysis cited by Wikipedia found 776 supplements with unlisted pharmaceutical ingredients, and reported that muscle-building supplements were contaminated with anabolic steroids [5].
No studies found. The published literature consists of analytical studies on identification and urinary detection [2][4].

timeline.event: A seized product sold as "1-Androsterone" is identified chemically and its urinary elimination described [2].
